messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands finance segment  - a few PMs asked about contingency reserves, cost centers, and whether we can shift some spend from opex to capex for tax/timing reasons. Can someone clarify?

maria: Short version: contingency reserve = a centralized buffer we hold for unplanned infra or legal costs. Currently target = 6% of annual operating spend, held in cash. Moving OPEX to CAPEX requires both accounting justification and procurement/legal alignment (e.g., multi-year prepayment or hardware purchase). We don't encourage creative reclassification just to meet runway targets.

eng_maya: Are chargebacks to product teams changing? We have confusion on how embeddings/storage costs show up in team budgets.

ops_jordan: Not changing today: infra & cloud usage are tagged by cost center. Heads up: we will publish a short mapping doc this week that explains tag -> cost-center -> product chargeback cadence (monthly). If teams want a bespoke internal chargeback cadence, reach out to ops and finance.

ceo_ana: To add: we want transparent internal pricing so PMs can make build vs buy tradeoffs. If a team is proposing Dedicated reservations, include an internal cost comparison in the PRD. We may fund strategic bets from a separate "strategic fund" rather than regular budget.

cfo_lee: A couple of accounting notes: 1) For capex treatment of cloud commitments we amortize over the commitment period. 2) Tax treatment varies by jurisdiction; we work with external tax to confirm. 3) Reclassification windows: changes to classification should be requested before month close.

alex: What about delayed vendor payments / negotiating payment terms to smooth cash? Any limits?

maria: Procurement negotiates terms. We will consider net-45/60 for strategic vendors. Finance must sign off on cash-flow impact. We won't extend terms that materially increase default risk. Use vendor-ops@redwood.com + cc finance-ops.

eng_maya: If a vendor only accepts card and amount > $5k, is there a preferred workaround?

maria: We prefer invoice routing. If vendor requires card, procurement can issue a virtual card after manager + finance approval; prefer to avoid for >$20k since audit trails get messy.

cfo_lee: Also: we're starting a quarterly review of high-spend vendors to find consolidation opportunities and renegotiate discounts. Expect outreach from procurement in the next 2 weeks.

ops_jordan: Teams asked about running a small pilot to prepay 12 months of a SaaS at a discount and classify as capex. Is that allowed?

maria: Allowed but needs a business case + approval. Prepayments > $25k need FP&A + legal review; we also need to model the amortization and the cash-flow hit.

ceo_ana: On hiring: we still aim for an 18-month baseline runway but will maintain a small headroom. We prefer targeted slowdowns to broad freezes. There's a new "priority hire" escrow process the execs will use for mission-critical roles.

alex: Any changes to procurement SLA? We had some delays on SOW reviews last month.

maria: Procurement SLA update: standard PO/invoice flow = 3 business days triage, SOW/legal review = up to 10 business days depending on complexity. For production-impacting purchases use the "expedite" flag and email finance-ops for priority handling.

eng_maya: What about FX exposure for vendors invoiced in EUR / GBP? Could that affect our runway if rates move?

cfo_lee: Great question. We monitor FX exposure. For material multi-month commitments we hedge or negotiate currency clauses. Procurement will flag material FX risk in the intake form.

alex: Any new action items coming out of this thread?

maria: Action items: 1) Publish "contingency reserve & classification primer" by Wed EOD. 2) Share cost-center tag mapping + chargeback cadence by Fri. 3) Publish updated procurement SLA + expedite instructions by next Tue. 4) Procurement to start vendor consolidation outreach within 2 weeks.

finance-bot: New ticket created: PROC-450 - Contingency primer + SLA updates (assigned to procurement).

ops_jordan: Thanks  I'll circulate to PMs and eng leads.

alex: Thanks everyone, helpful. Will follow up with any role-specific questions in the intake form. :white_check_mark:
